_comment: BUG-002 investigation, follow-up to step 5 (bug-reports/BUG-002-...md): identical wiring/profile to single_channel_bidirectional_600 (one bidirectional motor, channel 1, held at throttle 100) - the configuration that has NEVER reproduced BUG-002 - except core1_interval_us pads Core 1's tick to roughly the two-bidirectional-motor case's natural period (~366us average / 448us worst per ADR-002, both above AM32's ~360us DSHOT600 mid-frame-capture rejection limit from AM32_SOURCE_VERIFICATION.md finding/section 1). One bidirectional motor's own update() cost is ~175us, so 250us of padding targets a ~400-425us tick, comfortably in the range that step 5 (two bidirectional pairs, one idle) shared with every fully-failing scenario. If THIS reproduces BUG-002 with no second bidirectional motor at all, the tick period alone is the trigger. If it does not, something else specific to running two bidirectional TX/RX pairs concurrently is required beyond a slow tick - e.g. a shared IRQ/PIO timing interaction. duration_ms raised from the base scenario's 8s to 20s to give a delayed transition (seen up to 4.45s in prior instances) room to show up.
